chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Jameela, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
regarding a sheep that drank wine until it became intoxicated, then was slaughtered in that state. He said: 'Do not eat what is in her belly.'

key_terms.بَطْنِهَا: her belly — the stomach/belly contents that are forbidden
key_terms.خَمْراً: khamr — wine, an intoxicating beverage explicitly forbidden in Islam
key_terms.ذُبِحَتْ: was slaughtered — ritual slaughter (dhabh) performed on the intoxicated animal
key_terms.سَكِرَتْ: became intoxicated — the animal reached a state of intoxication
key_terms.شَاةٍ: sheep — the subject of the legal question

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat the stomach contents of a sheep that was intoxicated with wine before slaughter?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) issues a jurisprudential ruling that the stomach contents of a sheep which was intoxicated at the time of slaughter are forbidden to eat. This ruling addresses the ritual purity and permissibility of the internal organs and stomach contents of an animal that had consumed an intoxicant before being slaughtered. The hadith reflects the broader Shia principle that the effects of haram substances on an animal can render parts of it impermissible for consumption.
